description: I’m Yousef, a Mechanical Engineering student passionate about space robotics. I’m developing a Lunar Ballistic Hopper with LERSA (Linear Electromagnetic Regenerative Shock Absorber) for crater exploration, supported by an interactive 3D Digital Twin (Three.js).
summary: LERSA (Linear Electromagnetic Regenerative Shock Absorber) is a contactless, energy-harvesting landing and mobility system paired with an interactive 3D physics Digital Twin designed to unlock safe lunar exploration inside steep South Pole craters and Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs). Wheeled rovers such as VIPER stall on slopes steeper than 20°–25°, struggle with obstacles over 0.25 m, and face freezing temperatures down to 40 K (−233 °C) where solar power is unavailable. Our ballistic crater hopper overcomes 35°–42° crater walls using automated slope-adaptive launch trajectories (θ = 45° + α/2) while LERSA replaces single-use crushable dampers and bouncy mechanical springs with a Sm₂Co₁₇ Halbach magnet array moving through 11 copper stator coils. Upon touchdown, contactless electromagnetic damping absorbs impact shock without lubricants and converts kinetic energy into electricity. A dual-path power bus routes pulses into supercapacitors to charge the Li-ion battery while diverting overflow into ceramic shunt heaters to keep electronics above −20 °C. Calibrated with NASA LRO LOLA, Diviner, LCROSS, and VIPER datasets, our 3D Digital Twin lets mission planners compare landing sites, solar/Earth visibility, and damper performance in real time.
details: Our solution addresses the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge by combining an intuitive 3D interactive Digital Twin with a novel mechanical-electromagnetic landing architecture engineered for extreme South Pole crater environments: 1. Interactive 3D Digital Twin (1/240 s Deterministic Physics Solver): - Tab 1 (Lunar Mission & Terrain): Simulates realistic South Pole craters with 40 K PSR floors, volatile/ice zones, low-angle solar illumination (7°), and real-time Direct-to-Earth (DTE) line-of-sight raytracing. Includes a side-by-side NASA VIPER rover benchmark (0.2 m/s) demonstrating how wheeled rovers stall at 25° slopes while our hopper adapts its launch angle (θ = 45° + α/2) and deploys 3-axis reaction wheels and independent adaptive feet. - Tab 2 (LERSA Cross-Section): Live internal cutaway showing the Sm₂Co₁₇ Halbach magnet piston traversing 11 copper stator coils, coil glow proportional to induced current (e = −N·B·L·v), active reverse-current braking in the final 10% of stroke, and dual-path energy routing. - Tab 3 (Damper Comparison): Quantitative 4-way benchmark comparing LERSA against a Mechanical Spring, Ratchet Damper, and Crushable Honeycomb while enforcing lunar regolith bearing pressure limits (≤ 15 kPa) and avionics deceleration limits (≤ 20 g₀). 2. Cryogenic Electromagnetic & Thermal Engineering: - Lower temperatures inside PSRs reduce copper winding resistance (bounded conservatively at 0.2 R₀ in the solver), increasing damping coefficient c_em and energy conversion efficiency (up to 85%). - Harvested energy charges supercapacitors for the Li-ion bus, while excess pulse power feeds ceramic heaters coupled via a pitch-based carbon fiber thermal bridge to maintain avionics above −20 °C, supported by a zero-power passive rest latch. 3. Tools & Technologies Used: - HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), Three.js (3D WebGL visualization), Chart.js (real-time telemetry & damper comparison plots), and Python (data parameterization and engineering verification).
